definitions.gloss: somehow, for some reason, kind of
definitions.explanation: Expresses a vague feeling or impression that one cannot clearly explain. Used when the speaker senses something but cannot pinpoint the reason.

examples.japanese: {何|なん}だか{嫌|いや}な{予感|よかん}がする。
examples.english: I have a bad feeling for some reason.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{何|なん}だか{元気|げんき}が{出|で}ない。
examples.english: Today I just don't feel energetic for some reason.

notes:
{何|なん}だか expresses a vague, hard-to-define feeling. The speaker senses something but cannot clearly explain why. It often carries a slight emotional undertone.

FORMATION:
{何|なん} (what) + だ (copula) + か (question particle) — literally "what is it..." used adverbially to convey uncertainty.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {何|なん}だか{分|わ}からない: I don't know what it is / I can't tell
- {何|なん}だか{嬉|うれ}しい: I feel somehow happy
- {何|なん}だか{変|へん}だ: something seems odd

SIMILAR WORDS:
- なんとなく: vaguely, somehow (more neutral, less emotional)
- なぜか: for some reason (implies puzzlement, slightly more objective)
- どうも: somehow (wider range of uses, more formal)
- どことなく: in some indefinable way (literary)

REGISTER:
{何|なん}だか is conversational and informal. In writing or formal speech, なんとなく or どうも is preferred.
